reviews.summary: MPI scatters contiguous rank row and matching CSR intervals and rebases local row pointers. Timed host loop issues one GPU kernel per runtime iteration; the CPU outlined worker receives repeats, loops that bound with an OpenMP barrier per repetition, assigns all CPU rows, scans each CSR interval and stores. SASS assigns warps to GPU rows, each lane strides by 32 over the row's full [rowPtr,rowPtr+1) interval, reduces and stores lane 0; grid-stride row progression is present.

source_evidence.claim: CPU repeat/row/CSR loops; GPU warp/lane row and nonzero loops; MPI contiguous row/nnz partition and rebased pointers; timed GPU iterations plus CPU repeat call and synchronization.

compiled_evidence.claim: Runtime count controls GPU-stub launch loop; outlined worker receives the runtime count; worker loops repetitions through barrier, row assignments, CSR accumulation and stores, then host synchronizes before ending timing.
GPU row bound, lane-derived start, CSR chunk/remainder traversal, reduction/store and grid-stride row backedge in the final sm_86 image.

reviews.summary: Rows and corresponding CSR intervals are scattered per rank and local row pointers are rebased. SELL conversion packs every CSR element within each slice width (padding shorter rows); the selected timed kernel loops over packed width for each lane's row and writes the row output. The compiled out-of-line loop at f1eb increments r12, compares with runtime iterations and branches back around the kernel stub; device synchronization follows the loop. Final SASS bounds threads by rows, iterates slice-width products and stores outputs.

source_evidence.claim: SELL packing accounts for each row entry up to slice width; kernel consumes packed entries; MPI row/nnz distribution and timed runtime-count launches with sync.

compiled_evidence.claim: Clock boundaries enclose branch to out-of-line runtime counter loop; target f1eb increments/compares requested count and calls the SELL device stub before returning to synchronization.
Final kernel guards excess rows, traverses packed SELL row entries including its loop control, and stores output.

reviews.summary: Contiguous rank row partitions initialize the complete corresponding CSR entries. Before timing, long rows are copied in full into a separate CSR array and every short-row entry is packed into SELL. Every timed runtime-count pass launches the SELL kernel for short rows and the CSR kernel for long rows on separate streams; a device-wide synchronization completes both before the end timestamp. The SELL kernel traverses each original row length (not padded slice width); the long-row kernel multiplies every entry in 4096-entry chunks and sums the products. Both final SASS functions retain complete arithmetic and control.

source_evidence.claim: Long rows retain their nonzeros in CSR while short rows are packed to SELL; kernels cover their disjoint row groups; timed runOnce repeats requested count after optional untimed warmup.
CUDA/MPI/OpenMP build; optimized host/device compilation with separate device multiply/add rounding.

compiled_evidence.claim: Both compiled out-of-line launch branches are inside the runtime-count loop: SELL and conditional long-row launch in the normal nonempty-rank branch, plus the separate long-only branch. The requested count bounds repetition, followed by device-wide synchronization, MPI barrier and end clock.

Complete final long-row CSR and SELL kernel control: block-thread-strided products, shared-memory summation and 4096-entry outer progression for long rows; original row-length-bounded groups of eight and remainder work for short SELL rows; each kernel stores its disjoint row outputs.

reviews.notes: Work-preserving sparse-format conversion and long-row separation occur before timing. The short-row kernel does not multiply padding; it still multiplies every stored original nonzero. Retained as a methodological variation, not a work-count exclusion.
